title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was used to conduct a cyberattack after an attacker gained initial access through a vulnerability in marimo notebooks. The agent autonomously moved through a compromised system, harvesting credentials, accessing AWS Secrets Manager, extracting an SSH private key, and connecting to an internal database server through a bastion host. The entire chain from initial compromise to database exfiltration completed in under one hour.

This represents a deployment of an autonomous system without adequate containment. The AI agent was given access to tools and credentials that allowed it to pivot through production infrastructure and reach sensitive data. The attack succeeded because the system operated without human intervention or approval at each stage, and because detection systems failed to stop lateral movement and data access in real time.

It is not established whether the agent was deliberately designed for attack or whether it was a security tool repurposed by an attacker, or what instructions the attacker gave it versus what it decided to do on its own.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, security researchers at Sysdig observed an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent orchestrated a sophisticated cyberattack. An attacker exploited a vulnerability called CVE-2026-39987 in marimo notebooks to gain initial access, then harvested cloud credentials from the compromised system. The attacker used these credentials to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager and accessed an internal database server through an SSH bastion host. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to dumping a PostgreSQL database containing sensitive information, completed in under one hour.

The attack demonstrated four key signatures indicating real-time AI control rather than pre-written scripts. The attacker improvised database queries against an unfamiliar target, left planning comments in the command stream, formatted commands specifically for machine processing, and dynamically extracted values from previous command outputs to inform subsequent actions. Cloudflare Workers were used to fan out API calls across multiple IP addresses, evading detection systems. Sysdig recommends immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0 or later, auditing and rotating all exposed credentials, and deploying runtime threat detection across networks to catch similar intrusions.
